usageNotes: Retrieves the timezone configured inside the guest OS via the QEMU Guest Agent. Requires the Guest Agent to be installed, running, and connected inside the VM — the call will fail if the agent is offline or the VM is not running. Useful for verifying guest timezone alignment across a fleet before scheduling maintenance windows or cron jobs.

examples.summary: Get the timezone of VM 101 on node pve1

tips: The QEMU Guest Agent must be installed (qemu-guest-agent package) and enabled in the VM hardware settings — check Proxmox UI under Options > QEMU Guest Agent.
The returned `result` object contains the timezone string as reported by the guest OS (e.g., 'America/Los_Angeles' on Linux, or a Windows timezone name on Windows guests).
If the guest agent is not running, the API returns a 500-level error; use get_nodes_node_qemu_vmid_agent to check agent status first.
